title: Alginate hydrogel co-loaded with phellodendron bark extract and HucMSC-exosomes for combined antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and pro-repair acne effects
content:
by Yu He, Yu Wang, Yaofeng Zhi, Minxian Li, Meimei Wu, Yanyang Mai, Jiadi He, Jiaqin Chen, KwanNin To, Meigong Zhong, Xiaohong Ruan, Wanli Zuo, Yanming Huang, Liping Liang, MengDie Ou, Guohua Cheng, Xin Zhang

Acne vulgaris is a common inflammatory skin disorder involving follicular hyperkeratosis, Cutibacterium acnes proliferation, and aberrant inflammation, often leading to scarring. Current antibiotic treatments face resistance and limited repair capacity. Here, we developed an alginate-based hydrogel co-loaded with Phellodendron bark extract (PBE) and human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (HucMSC-Exo) (PE gel). Antibacterial activity of PBE was evaluated against C. acnes, S. aureus, and E. coli. Drug release and in vitro durability were characterized. A rat ear acne model assessed swelling resolution, bacterial load, histopathology, and inflammatory/repair-related markers. PBE exhibited potent broad-spectrum antibacterial activity (MIC ~ 5 mg/mL against C. acnes), which was retained in the presence of exosomes. Zeta potential showed a bimodal distribution, indicating the coexistence of distinct particle populations. PE gel sustained PBE release ≥24 h and prolonged antibacterial activity >72 h. In vivo, PE gel achieved 74.9% ear swelling resolution on day 11, reduced bacterial load >99.8%, lowered follicular hyperkeratosis to 11.2%, and increased collagen maturity to 73.4%. PBE suppressed TNF-α/IL-6, while exosomes enhanced VEGF/CD31-mediated angiogenesis and collagen remodeling. PE gel may help disrupt the acne pathological cycle through a combined antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and pro-repair effects, representing a potential non-antibiotic strategy for acne management.
